rows.stem: If in the given figure, \(\angle C = \angle D = 90^\circ\), \(\angle B = 60^\circ\) and AP = 3 cm, then the area of the shaded region is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - quadrilateral ABCD with right angles at C and D and the 60 degree angle at B; the shaded region is the sector centred at A with radius AP = 3 cm (P on DA) bounded by AD and AB, which only the drawing defines. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
CD is perpendicular to both CB and DA (\(\angle C = \angle D = 90^\circ\)), so \(CB \parallel DA\). The co-interior angles at B and A then add up to \(180^\circ\): \(\angle A = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\).

The shaded region is a sector of the circle centred at A with radius \(AP = 3\) cm and angle \(120^\circ\).

Area \(= \dfrac{120}{360} \times \pi \times 3^2 = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 9\pi = 3\pi\ \text{cm}^2\), which is option (A) \(3\pi\) cm\(^2\).

From the letters of the word “MOBILE”, a letter is selected at random. The probability that the selected letter is a vowel, is :
rows.solution:
The word MOBILE has 6 letters, and 3 of them (O, I, E) are vowels.

\(P(\text{vowel}) = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), which is option (C) \(\dfrac{1}{2}\).

rows.subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
rows.stem: A quadratic polynomial, one of whose zeroes is \(2 + \sqrt{5}\) and the sum of whose zeroes is 4, is :
rows.solution:
The other zero is \(4 - (2 + \sqrt{5}) = 2 - \sqrt{5}\).

Product of the zeroes \(= (2 + \sqrt{5})(2 - \sqrt{5}) = 4 - 5 = -1\).

The polynomial is \(x^2 - (\text{sum})x + \text{product} = x^2 - 4x - 1\), which is option (B) \(x^2 - 4x - 1\).

rows.stem: If the first three terms of an A.P. are \(3p - 1\), \(3p + 5\), \(5p + 1\) respectively; then the value of p is :
rows.solution:
In an A.P. the middle term is the average of its neighbours: \(2(3p + 5) = (3p - 1) + (5p + 1)\).

\(6p + 10 = 8p\), so \(p = 5\), which is option (D) \(5\).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: In a school, there are two sections of class X. There are 40 students in the first section and 48 students in the second section. Determine the minimum number of books required for their class library so that they can be distributed equally among students of both sections.
rows.solution:
The number of books must be divisible by both 40 and 48, so the minimum number is the LCM of 40 and 48.

\(40 = 2^3 \times 5\) and \(48 = 2^4 \times 3\), so LCM \(= 2^4 \times 3 \times 5 = 240\).

The minimum number of books required is 240.

rows.stem: If \(\sin\theta + \cos\theta = p\) and \(\sec\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta = q\), then prove that \(q(p^2 - 1) = 2p\).
rows.solution:
LHS \(= q(p^2 - 1) = (\sec\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta)[(\sin\theta + \cos\theta)^2 - 1]\).

\(\sec\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta = \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta} + \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta} = \dfrac{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\).

\((\sin\theta + \cos\theta)^2 - 1 = \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta - 1 = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\), since \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\).

So LHS \(= \dfrac{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} \times 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2(\sin\theta + \cos\theta) = 2p =\) RHS.

rows.stem: A man starts his job with a certain monthly salary and earns a fixed increment every year. If his salary was ₹ 15,000 after 4 years of service and ₹ 18,000 after 10 years of service, what was his starting salary and what was the annual increment ?
rows.solution:
His salaries in successive years form an A.P. Let his starting salary (the 1st term) be ₹ a and the annual increment ₹ d. The salary in the 4th year is the 4th term and the salary in the 10th year is the 10th term.

\(a_4 = a + 3d = 15000\) ... (i)

\(a_{10} = a + 9d = 18000\) ... (ii)

Subtracting (i) from (ii): \(6d = 3000\), so \(d = 500\). Then \(a = 15000 - 3 \times 500 = 13500\).

His starting salary was ₹ 13,500 and the annual increment was ₹ 500.

This follows the marking scheme, which takes "after 4 years" as the 4th term. If "after 4 years" is read as four increments already added (\(a + 4d = 15000\) and \(a + 10d = 18000\)), the starting salary comes out as ₹ 13,000; the increment, ₹ 500, is the same on both readings.

rows.subtopic: Nature of Roots and the Discriminant
rows.stem: Find the value of ‘k’ for which the quadratic equation \((k + 1)x^2 - 2(3k + 1)x + (8k + 1) = 0\) has real and equal roots.
rows.solution:
For real and equal roots the discriminant must be zero:

\([-2(3k + 1)]^2 - 4(k + 1)(8k + 1) = 0\).

\(4(9k^2 + 6k + 1) - 4(8k^2 + 9k + 1) = 0\), that is \(4(k^2 - 3k) = 0\).

\(k(k - 3) = 0\), so \(k = 0\) or \(k = 3\).

Both values keep the coefficient \(k + 1\) of \(x^2\) non-zero, so \(k = 0\) or \(k = 3\).

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: A 2-digit number is such that the product of its digits is 18. When 63 is subtracted from the number, the digits interchange their places. Find the number.
rows.solution:
Let the tens digit be x and the units digit be y, so the number is \(10x + y\).

The product of the digits is 18: \(xy = 18\) ... (i)

Subtracting 63 interchanges the digits: \((10x + y) - 63 = 10y + x\), so \(9x - 9y = 63\), that is \(x - y = 7\) ... (ii)

From (ii), \(x = y + 7\). Substituting in (i): \(y(y + 7) = 18\), so \(y^2 + 7y - 18 = 0\).

\((y + 9)(y - 2) = 0\), so \(y = 2\) or \(y = -9\). A digit cannot be negative, so \(y = 2\) and \(x = 9\).

The number is 92. (Check: \(9 \times 2 = 18\) and \(92 - 63 = 29\).)

rows.stem: The angles of depression of the top and the bottom of a 50 m high building from the top of a tower are \(45^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\), respectively. Find the height of the tower. (Use \(\sqrt{3} = 1{\cdot}73\))
rows.solution:
Let AB be the tower, H m high, and CD the building, 50 m high, with \(BD = x\) m. Draw CE parallel to BD, meeting AB at E, so \(EC = x\) m and \(AE = (H - 50)\) m.

The angles of depression from A equal the angles of elevation at the other end (alternate angles): \(\angle ADB = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle ACE = 45^\circ\).

In right triangle ABD: \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{H}{x} = \sqrt{3}\), so \(H = \sqrt{3}\,x\) ... (i)

In right triangle AEC: \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{H - 50}{x} = 1\), so \(x = H - 50\) ... (ii)

From (i) and (ii): \(H = \sqrt{3}(H - 50)\), so \(H(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 50\sqrt{3}\) and

\(H = \dfrac{50\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = \dfrac{50\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2} = 25(3 + \sqrt{3}) = 25(3 + 1{\cdot}73) = 118{\cdot}25\).

The height of the tower is \(118{\cdot}25\) m.
